reference_sql:
WITH views AS (
  -- one row per page_view from 1 to 15 December 2025
  SELECT list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'page_location')[1].value.string_value AS page_location
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'page_view'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251215'
)
SELECT split_part(replace(page_location, 'https://www.mailvora.example', ''), '?', 1) AS page_path,
  COUNT(*) AS page_views
FROM views
GROUP BY split_part(replace(page_location, 'https://www.mailvora.example', ''), '?', 1)
alternatives:
SELECT regexp_replace([p.value.string_value FOR p IN event_params IF p.key = 'page_location'][1], '^https://www[.]mailvora[.]example|[?].*$', '', 'g') AS page_path,
  COUNT(*) AS page_views
FROM events
WHERE event_name = 'page_view'
  AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251215'
GROUP BY 1

SELECT split_part(substring(p.value.string_value, 29), '?', 1) AS page_path, COUNT(*) AS page_views
FROM events AS e, unnest(e.event_params) AS t(p)
WHERE e.event_name = 'page_view'
  AND e.event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251215'
  AND p.key = 'page_location'
GROUP BY 1

other_way.tradeoff: Unnesting the list and keeping the page_location key works here, but it would drop a page_view that carries no page_location.

SELECT CASE WHEN length(split_part(replace(list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'page_location')[1].value.string_value, 'https://www.mailvora.example', ''), '?', 1)) = 0 THEN '/' ELSE split_part(replace(list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'page_location')[1].value.string_value, 'https://www.mailvora.example', ''), '?', 1) END AS page_path, COUNT(*) AS page_views
FROM events
WHERE event_name = 'page_view' AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251215'
GROUP BY 1
